prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1268; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the insured driver regarding a low-speed head-on collision in a parking area. Insured reports the other vehicle crossed into their lane during a turn. Both vehicles drivable. Claimant reports neck and lower back discomfort at the scene and has been advised to seek medical evaluation. Photos requested from the insured and posted to the file.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from the claimant. Claimant states they were seated normally, belt fastened, and felt a jolt on impact. Describes lower back strain with stiffness the following morning. Claimant confirms they are not represented by an attorney and is handling the claim directly. Explained the claims process and the right to obtain repair estimates from a shop of their choice.

Entry 3: Police report obtained. Reporting officer noted minor front-end damage to both vehicles, no airbag deployment, and no citations issued. Scene diagram consistent with the statements received so far. Liability review underway based on the diagram and the conflicting accounts of the turn.

Entry 4: Claimant provided medical documentation from an urgent care visit. Diagnosis listed as acute lumbar strain with a recommended course of rest, anti-inflammatory medication, and physical therapy referral. Records reviewed and logged. Requested a copy of the treatment plan and any work restrictions, if applicable, to evaluate the bodily injury component.

Entry 5: Repair estimates received for both vehicles and reviewed against the damage photos. Liability assessment pending a response from the other driver's carrier. Claimant informed that the injury evaluation will remain open until the physical therapy plan is complete. Follow-up call scheduled to confirm the claimant's current symptoms and the status of their treatment.
